term: no common part between complete cause and effect
definition: For each G.edge c e, no object p is part of both c and e, under the SAME fixed partial order and the existing common-part Overlap. This is stronger than numerical distinction or merely not being part of the effect.
note: This raw graph policy has no world-indexed actuality guards, unlike CauseEffectNonoverlapAt. Rutten p135 argues from ontological priority; that defense is attributed, not established by order logic. Constitutive parts overlap their wholes, so the relation cannot silently be all ontological grounding.
